shots.focal_element: The Bug Tracker database table, specifically the Assignee column filling in
shots.typography: Native Notion database UI shown large: bold sans page title, regular sans row text and column headers in grey, small rounded status pills and priority tags; sentence case, default tracking. 'Priorit' header is cropped by the frame edge.
shots.what_happens: Tight full-bleed view of a 7-row bug table; over ~2 s the empty Assignee cells populate one by one top to bottom (Jordan Scales, then Luca Beetz rows, then Chloe Chau and Kameron Shiller) with avatar plus name, showing the agent assigning owners. A chime SFX (x031) lands inside this shot.
shots.build_rebuild: Render a static table component cropped full-frame and stagger-reveal the missing assignee cells (avatar + name, quick fade) row by row at roughly 0.25 s intervals, with a chime on the first fill.

shots.focal_element: The agent prompt box with the hatted agent avatar, then the Bug Tracker's first row being clicked
on_screen_text: What can I wrangle up for ya?
...AND write a summary for each bug
shots.typography: Simplified Notion AI input on off-white: semibold sans greeting heading in sentence case, regular sans typed prompt with a text caret and emphasis via uppercase 'AND', small grey mention chip and toolbar labels; then native Notion table type (bold title, regular rows, rounded status pills).
shots.what_happens: The cowboy-hat agent avatar asks 'What can I wrangle up for ya?' above a blue-outlined prompt card already @-mentioning 'Bug Tracking Dashboard'; the follow-up prompt types on ('...AND write a summary for each bug' plus a praying-hands emoji), the cursor clicks the blue send button, then the view changes (around 55.5 s, within the shot) to the Bug Tracker table, which slides/settles as the cursor moves onto and selects the first row 'PDF export feature generates...' (blue row outline).
shots.build_rebuild: Centre a rounded, soft-shadowed input card with a blue 2px border under an avatar+heading row, typewriter the prompt text with a blinking caret, animate a cursor to the round send button with a press scale, then dissolve to a table screenshot and draw a blue outline around the first row when the cursor reaches it.

shots.focal_element: Bug Tracking Dashboard window with the opened side-peek page 'PDF export feature generates corrupted files'
on_screen_text: Log new bugs directly below or paste links to messages, issues, or emails
Keep Status and Priority up to date
PDF export feature generates corrupted files
PDF file is corrupted and cannot be opened
Clean, readable PDF with proper formatting

The PDF export functionality across all reporting modules is generating corrupted files that cannot be opened by any PDF reader. This is a high-priority production issue affecting customer deliverables.
Sales Reports: Working (generated via different service)
shots.typography: Native Notion UI in a browser window: bold sans page titles, small grey property labels, regular sans values and body copy with bold inline emphasis ('corrupted files', 'high-priority production issue'), coloured tag pills; sentence case, default tracking. Text is small at this scale and some lines are partly cut off at the window bottom.
shots.what_happens: Wide view of the whole dashboard window on the saturated blue backdrop: the table on the left with the first row highlighted, and the agent-written bug page open in a right-hand side peek (properties, Issue Overview, Affected Reports with check/cross emoji). The view holds for ~2 s, then a 'Bug Catchers Bi-Weekly Meeting' notification with a blue 'Transcribe' button slides in at the top right, and by the last sampled frame (60.0 s) the framing has already pushed in tightly on that notification and the bug page title.
shots.build_rebuild: Show a soft-shadowed browser-chrome window (~88% width) on a solid blue background with a split table/side-peek layout, hold, then slide a rounded notification card down from the top-right and ease a fast camera push-in toward it in the final ~0.3 s.

shots.focal_element: The meeting notification card and its blue 'Transcribe' button under the cursor
on_screen_text: PDF export feature generates corrupted files
PDF file is corrupted and cannot be opened
shots.typography: Large Notion UI sans: medium-weight notification title, grey regular 'Created in' line with underlined link, white semibold label on the blue button with the Notion 'N' icon; bold page title below; sentence case.
shots.what_happens: Close-up (about 1.3 s) on the floating notification overlapping the bug page; the cursor sits on 'Transcribe' and clicks it (cursor shifts slightly down between frames), starting meeting transcription.
shots.build_rebuild: Crop to the top-right of the page at ~2x, keep a shadowed notification card on top with a blue split button, and animate the cursor pressing the button with a brief scale-down on click.

shots.focal_element: Audio waveform, then the meeting-notes Transcript card streaming text next to a headset-wearing agent avatar
on_screen_text: Can everyone hear me? No? Yes. Okay. Let's wait a minute for everyone to join before we jump in. Quick reminder that we're here today to discuss any last minute bugs before launch — thank you so much for joining us!
shots.typography: Simplified Notion meeting-notes card on off-white: small grey sans tab labels with the active 'Transcript' tab in a grey pill, red 'Stop' pill, medium-weight sans title with grey '@Today' mention, regular sans body quote with a left rule; sentence case. The newest word appears in faded grey before resolving to black.
shots.what_happens: Opens on large grey rounded waveform bars pulsing on white (~1.5 s), then cuts within the shot to a transcript card whose live mini-waveform runs in the header while the quote streams in word by word; a headset agent avatar sits overlapping the card's bottom-right corner. Real speech is heard here (w0-w7 'Thank you so much to all of you.' at 63.66-65.30 s), which roughly matches but is not identical to the on-screen line 'thank you so much for joining us!'.
shots.build_rebuild: Animate ~13 vertical rounded bars with sinusoidal height offsets, then swap to a shadowed card with tabs and a 'Stop' pill and stream the transcript text in word by word (new words fade from light grey to black) synced to a speech clip, with an SVG avatar badge pinned over the card's bottom-right corner.
